## `tv/android-tv/tools/verify_apk.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verify a ZeroPlay TV APK before it is offered for sideloading.

This is deliberately TV-specific rather than a reuse of the old SavageBrowser
checks. It verifies the package identity, ARMv7 native-library contract,
Leanback manifest contract, DEX integrity, ZIP alignment, launcher assets and,
when Android SDK tools are available, aapt2/apksigner/zipalign results.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import zipfile
import zlib
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable

EXPECTED_PACKAGE = "com.savage.zeroplay.tv"
EXPECTED_MAIN_ACTIVITY = "com.savage.zeroplay.tv.MainActivity"
EXPECTED_MIN_SDK = 26
EXPECTED_TARGET_SDK = 34
ALLOWED_ABIS = {"armeabi-v7a"}
REQUIRED_PERMISSIONS = {
    "android.permission.INTERNET",
    "android.permission.ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE",
}


def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as handle:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def png_size(data: bytes) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    if len(data) < 24 or not data.startswith(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n") or data[12:16] != b"IHDR":
        return None
    return struct.unpack(">II", data[16:24])


def webp_size(data: bytes) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    """Return dimensions for the VP8, VP8L and VP8X WebP layouts AAPT2 emits."""
    if len(data) < 30 or data[:4] != b"RIFF" or data[8:12] != b"WEBP":
        return None
    chunk = data[12:16]
    if chunk == b"VP8X":
        width = int.from_bytes(data[24:27], "little") + 1
        height = int.from_bytes(data[27:30], "little") + 1
        return width, height
    if chunk == b"VP8L" and data[20] == 0x2F:
        bits = int.from_bytes(data[21:25], "little")
        return (bits & 0x3FFF) + 1, ((bits >> 14) & 0x3FFF) + 1
    if chunk == b"VP8 " and data[23:26] == b"\x9d\x01\x2a":
        width = struct.unpack_from("<H", data, 26)[0] & 0x3FFF
        height = struct.unpack_from("<H", data, 28)[0] & 0x3FFF
        return width, height
    return None


def jpeg_size(data: bytes) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    if len(data) < 4 or data[:2] != b"\xff\xd8":
        return None
    index = 2
    sof_markers = {0xC0, 0xC1, 0xC2, 0xC3, 0xC5, 0xC6, 0xC7, 0xC9, 0xCA, 0xCB, 0xCD, 0xCE, 0xCF}
    while index + 9 < len(data):
        if data[index] != 0xFF:
            index += 1
            continue
        marker = data[index + 1]
        if marker in (0xD8, 0x01) or 0xD0 <= marker <= 0xD7:
            index += 2
            continue
        length = struct.unpack_from(">H", data, index + 2)[0]
        if length < 2:
            return None
        if marker in sof_markers:
            height, width = struct.unpack_from(">HH", data, index + 5)
            return width, height
        index += 2 + length
    return None


def image_size(data: bytes) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    return png_size(data) or webp_size(data) or jpeg_size(data)


def candidate_sdk_roots() -> list[Path]:
    roots: list[Path] = []
    for env_name in ("ANDROID_HOME", "ANDROID_SDK_ROOT"):
        value = os.environ.get(env_name)
        if value:
            roots.append(Path(value))
    roots.extend([
        Path("/usr/local/lib/android/sdk"),
        Path.home() / "Android" / "Sdk",
        Path.home() / "Library" / "Android" / "sdk",
    ])
    out: list[Path] = []
    for root in roots:
        if root not in out:
            out.append(root)
    return out


def find_sdk_tool(name: str) -> str | None:
    found = shutil.which(name)
    if found:
        return found
    suffixes = ["", ".bat", ".exe"] if os.name == "nt" else [""]
    candidates: list[Path] = []
    for root in candidate_sdk_roots():
        build_tools = root / "build-tools"
        if build_tools.is_dir():
            for version_dir in build_tools.iterdir():
                for suffix in suffixes:
                    candidate = version_dir / f"{name}{suffix}"
                    if candidate.is_file():
                        candidates.append(candidate)
        for relative in (Path("platform-tools"), Path("cmdline-tools/latest/bin")):
            for suffix in suffixes:
                candidate = root / relative / f"{name}{suffix}"
                if candidate.is_file():
                    candidates.append(candidate)
    if not candidates:
        return None
    # The highest build-tools directory sorts last for normal numeric releases.
    return str(sorted(candidates)[-1])


def run_tool(args: list[str]) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    return subprocess.run(args, text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, check=False)


def contains_binary_text(data: bytes, text: str) -> bool:
    return text.encode("utf-8") in data or text.encode("utf-16le") in data


def verify(apk_path: Path, require_sdk_tools: bool = False) -> dict:
    errors: list[str] = []
    warnings: list[str] = []
    metrics: dict[str, object] = {
        "apk": str(apk_path),
        "expected_package": EXPECTED_PACKAGE,
        "expected_main_activity": EXPECTED_MAIN_ACTIVITY,
        "allowed_native_abis": sorted(ALLOWED_ABIS),
    }
    if not apk_path.is_file():
        return {"passed": False, "errors": [f"APK not found: {apk_path}"], "warnings": warnings, "metrics": metrics}

    metrics["size_bytes"] = apk_path.stat().st_size
    metrics["sha256"] = sha256_file(apk_path)

    names: list[str] = []
    resource_images: list[str] = []
    banner_entries: list[str] = []
    icon_entries: list[str] = []
    banner_verified = False
    icon_verified = False
    banner_invalid_reported = False
    icon_invalid_reported = False
    try:
        with apk_path.open("rb") as raw, zipfile.ZipFile(raw) as zf:
            bad_file = zf.testzip()
            if bad_file:
                errors.append(f"Corrupt ZIP entry: {bad_file}")
            infos = zf.infolist()
            names = [info.filename for info in infos]
            metrics["file_count"] = len(names)

            for required in ("AndroidManifest.xml", "classes.dex", "resources.arsc", "assets/offline.html"):
                if required not in names:
                    errors.append(f"Missing required APK entry: {required}")

            native_libs = sorted(name for name in names if name.startswith("lib/") and name.endswith(".so"))
            native_abis = sorted({name.split("/")[1] for name in native_libs if len(name.split("/")) > 2})
            metrics["native_libraries"] = native_libs
            metrics["native_library_abis"] = native_abis
            disallowed = sorted(set(native_abis) - ALLOWED_ABIS)
            if disallowed:
                errors.append(f"Native libraries use disallowed ABIs for the target box: {', '.join(disallowed)}")

            if "classes.dex" in names:
                dex = zf.read("classes.dex")
                metrics["dex_size_bytes"] = len(dex)
                if len(dex) < 112 or not dex.startswith(b"dex\n"):
                    errors.append("classes.dex has an invalid DEX header")
                else:
                    stored_checksum = struct.unpack_from("<I", dex, 8)[0]
                    computed_checksum = zlib.adler32(dex[12:]) & 0xFFFFFFFF
                    if stored_checksum != computed_checksum:
                        errors.append("classes.dex Adler-32 checksum does not match its contents")
                    stored_signature = dex[12:32]
                    computed_signature = hashlib.sha1(dex[32:]).digest()
                    if stored_signature != computed_signature:
                        errors.append("classes.dex SHA-1 signature does not match its contents")

            manifest = zf.read("AndroidManifest.xml") if "AndroidManifest.xml" in names else b""
            fallback_checks = {
                "package": EXPECTED_PACKAGE,
                "activity": ".MainActivity",
                "Leanback launcher": "android.intent.category.LEANBACK_LAUNCHER",
                "Leanback feature": "android.software.leanback",
                "Internet permission": "android.permission.INTERNET",
                "Network state permission": "android.permission.ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE",
            }
            metrics["binary_manifest_fallback"] = {
                label: contains_binary_text(manifest, needle) for label, needle in fallback_checks.items()
            }
            for label, present in metrics["binary_manifest_fallback"].items():
                if not present:
                    warnings.append(f"Binary-manifest fallback did not find {label}; SDK XML output is authoritative when available")

            resource_images = [name for name in names
                               if name.startswith("res/") and "/" in name
                               and name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() in {"png", "webp", "jpg", "jpeg"}]
            # Release resource optimization may shorten compiled paths from
            # res/drawable-xhdpi-v4/tv_banner.png to res/FS.png. Named paths
            # are therefore only the first identification route; AAPT badging
            # below is authoritative for optimized resource names.
            banner_entries = [name for name in resource_images if "/tv_banner." in name]
            icon_entries = [name for name in resource_images if "/ic_launcher." in name]
            resource_image_sizes = {name: image_size(zf.read(name)) for name in resource_images}
            metrics["resource_image_entries"] = resource_images
            metrics["resource_image_sizes"] = resource_image_sizes
            metrics["tv_banner_entries"] = banner_entries
            metrics["launcher_icon_entries"] = icon_entries
            banner_verified = bool(banner_entries)
            for banner in banner_entries:
                dimensions = resource_image_sizes.get(banner)
                metrics.setdefault("tv_banner_sizes", {})[banner] = dimensions
                if dimensions != (320, 180):
                    banner_verified = False
                    banner_invalid_reported = True
                    errors.append(f"TV banner {banner} is {dimensions}, expected (320, 180)")
            icon_verified = bool(icon_entries)
            for icon in icon_entries:
                dimensions = resource_image_sizes.get(icon)
                metrics.setdefault("launcher_icon_sizes", {})[icon] = dimensions
                if not dimensions or dimensions[0] != dimensions[1] or dimensions[0] < 48:
                    icon_verified = False
                    icon_invalid_reported = True
                    errors.append(f"Launcher icon {icon} has invalid dimensions {dimensions}")

            for info in infos:
                if info.compress_type != zipfile.ZIP_STORED:
                    continue
                raw.seek(info.header_offset)
                header = raw.read(30)
                if len(header) != 30 or header[:4] != b"PK\x03\x04":
                    warnings.append(f"Could not inspect ZIP local header for {info.filename}")
                    continue
                name_len, extra_len = struct.unpack_from("<HH", header, 26)
                data_offset = info.header_offset + 30 + name_len + extra_len
                if data_offset % 4:
                    errors.append(f"Stored ZIP entry is not 4-byte aligned: {info.filename} at {data_offset}")
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - verifier must report malformed archives.
        errors.append(f"Could not inspect APK ZIP: {exc}")

    aapt2 = find_sdk_tool("aapt2") or find_sdk_tool("aapt")
    apksigner = find_sdk_tool("apksigner")
    zipalign = find_sdk_tool("zipalign")
    metrics["sdk_tools"] = {"aapt": aapt2, "apksigner": apksigner, "zipalign": zipalign}

    if require_sdk_tools:
        for label, tool in (("aapt2/aapt", aapt2), ("apksigner", apksigner), ("zipalign", zipalign)):
            if not tool:
                errors.append(f"Required Android SDK tool not found: {label}")
    else:
        for label, tool in (("aapt2/aapt", aapt2), ("apksigner", apksigner), ("zipalign", zipalign)):
            if not tool:
                warnings.append(f"Android SDK tool not found, skipped: {label}")

    if aapt2:
        badging = run_tool([aapt2, "dump", "badging", str(apk_path)])
        metrics["aapt_badging_exit"] = badging.returncode
        if badging.returncode != 0:
            errors.append("aapt dump badging failed")
            warnings.append(badging.stdout[-1000:])
        else:
            output = badging.stdout
            package_match = re.search(r"package: name='([^']+)' versionCode='([^']*)' versionName='([^']*)'", output)
            if package_match:
                metrics["package"] = package_match.group(1)
                metrics["version_code"] = package_match.group(2)
                metrics["version_name"] = package_match.group(3)
                if package_match.group(1) != EXPECTED_PACKAGE:
                    errors.append(f"Package mismatch: {package_match.group(1)}")
            else:
                errors.append("aapt badging did not report package/version")
            sdk_match = re.search(r"sdkVersion:'(\d+)'", output)
            target_match = re.search(r"targetSdkVersion:'(\d+)'", output)
            if sdk_match:
                metrics["min_sdk"] = int(sdk_match.group(1))
                if metrics["min_sdk"] != EXPECTED_MIN_SDK:
                    errors.append(f"Min SDK mismatch: {metrics['min_sdk']}")
            if target_match:
                metrics["target_sdk"] = int(target_match.group(1))
                if metrics["target_sdk"] != EXPECTED_TARGET_SDK:
                    errors.append(f"Target SDK mismatch: {metrics['target_sdk']}")
            native_match = re.search(r"native-code: ([^\n]+)", output)
            if native_match:
                badging_abis = re.findall(r"'([^']+)'", native_match.group(1))
                metrics["aapt_native_code"] = badging_abis
                if set(badging_abis) - ALLOWED_ABIS:
                    errors.append(f"aapt reports disallowed native ABIs: {badging_abis}")
            permissions = set(re.findall(r"uses-permission: name='([^']+)'", output))
            metrics["permissions"] = sorted(permissions)
            missing_permissions = REQUIRED_PERMISSIONS - permissions
            if missing_permissions:
                errors.append(f"Missing required permissions: {sorted(missing_permissions)}")
            unexpected_permissions = permissions - REQUIRED_PERMISSIONS
            if unexpected_permissions:
                warnings.append(f"Unexpected permissions present: {sorted(unexpected_permissions)}")

            # AAPT badging reports the actual compiled banner/icon paths,
            # including the shortened res/xx.png names produced by release
            # resource optimization. Use those paths when source basenames
            # did not survive compilation.
            badging_banner_paths: list[str] = []
            banner_match = re.search(r"^application:.*?\bbanner='([^']+)'", output, re.M)
            if banner_match:
                badging_banner_paths.append(banner_match.group(1))
            badging_icon_paths: list[str] = []
            application_icon = re.search(r"^application:.*?\bicon='([^']+)'", output, re.M)
            if application_icon:
                badging_icon_paths.append(application_icon.group(1))
            badging_icon_paths.extend(
                re.findall(r"^application-icon-\d+:'([^']+)'", output, re.M))
            badging_banner_paths = list(dict.fromkeys(badging_banner_paths))
            badging_icon_paths = list(dict.fromkeys(badging_icon_paths))
            metrics["aapt_banner_entries"] = badging_banner_paths
            metrics["aapt_launcher_icon_entries"] = badging_icon_paths
            try:
                with zipfile.ZipFile(apk_path) as zf:
                    for banner in badging_banner_paths:
                        if banner not in names:
                            banner_invalid_reported = True
                            errors.append(f"AAPT banner path is not present in the APK: {banner}")
                            continue
                        if banner not in banner_entries:
                            banner_entries.append(banner)
                        dimensions = image_size(zf.read(banner))
                        metrics.setdefault("tv_banner_sizes", {})[banner] = dimensions
                        if dimensions == (320, 180):
                            banner_verified = True
                        else:
                            banner_invalid_reported = True
                            errors.append(f"TV banner {banner} is {dimensions}, expected (320, 180)")
                    badging_icons_valid = bool(badging_icon_paths)
                    for icon in badging_icon_paths:
                        if icon not in names:
                            badging_icons_valid = False
                            icon_invalid_reported = True
                            errors.append(f"AAPT launcher icon path is not present in the APK: {icon}")
                            continue
                        if icon not in icon_entries:
                            icon_entries.append(icon)
                        dimensions = image_size(zf.read(icon))
                        metrics.setdefault("launcher_icon_sizes", {})[icon] = dimensions
                        if not dimensions or dimensions[0] != dimensions[1] or dimensions[0] < 48:
                            badging_icons_valid = False
                            icon_invalid_reported = True
                            errors.append(f"Launcher icon {icon} has invalid dimensions {dimensions}")
                    if badging_icons_valid:
                        icon_verified = True
                metrics["tv_banner_entries"] = banner_entries
                metrics["launcher_icon_entries"] = icon_entries
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - report malformed archives.
                errors.append(f"Could not inspect AAPT-reported launcher images: {exc}")

        # aapt and aapt2 use different xmltree syntax: aapt takes the
        # compiled XML name as a positional file, while aapt2 requires
        # --file. Calling aapt2 the aapt way makes it look for a second APK.
        xmltree_args = [aapt2, "dump", "xmltree", str(apk_path)]
        if Path(aapt2).name.lower().startswith("aapt2"):
            xmltree_args += ["--file", "AndroidManifest.xml"]
        else:
            xmltree_args.append("AndroidManifest.xml")
        xmltree = run_tool(xmltree_args)
        metrics["aapt_xmltree_exit"] = xmltree.returncode
        metrics["aapt_xmltree_command"] = xmltree_args
        if xmltree.returncode != 0:
            errors.append("aapt dump xmltree failed for AndroidManifest.xml")
            warnings.append(xmltree.stdout[-1000:])
        else:
            xml = xmltree.stdout
            for label, needle in (
                ("MainActivity", ".MainActivity"),
                ("Leanback launcher category", "android.intent.category.LEANBACK_LAUNCHER"),
                ("Leanback feature", "android.software.leanback"),
                # Compiled resource references may be printed as numeric IDs,
                # so prove the banner attribute here and prove the actual
                # 320x180 tv_banner.png entry in the ZIP checks above.
                ("TV banner attribute", "android:banner"),
            ):
                if needle not in xml:
                    errors.append(f"Compiled manifest does not contain {label}: {needle}")
            if 'android.hardware.touchscreen' in xml and 'required(0x010102bd)=true' in xml:
                warnings.append("Touchscreen appears in the manifest; confirm it remains optional in aapt feature output")

    if apksigner:
        signed = run_tool([apksigner, "verify", "--verbose", "--print-certs", str(apk_path)])
        metrics["apksigner_exit"] = signed.returncode
        if signed.returncode != 0:
            errors.append("apksigner verification failed")
            warnings.append(signed.stdout[-1000:])
        else:
            output = signed.stdout
            metrics["signature_schemes"] = {
                "v1": bool(re.search(r"Verified using v1 scheme.*true", output, re.I)),
                "v2": bool(re.search(r"Verified using v2 scheme.*true", output, re.I)),
                "v3": bool(re.search(r"Verified using v3 scheme.*true", output, re.I)),
                "v4": bool(re.search(r"Verified using v4 scheme.*true", output, re.I)),
            }
            if not (metrics["signature_schemes"]["v2"] or metrics["signature_schemes"]["v3"]):
                errors.append("APK is not verified with signature scheme v2 or v3")
            cert_match = re.search(r"Signer #1 certificate DN: (.+)", output)
            if cert_match:
                metrics["signer_certificate_dn"] = cert_match.group(1).strip()

    if zipalign:
        aligned = run_tool([zipalign, "-c", "-v", "4", str(apk_path)])
        metrics["zipalign_exit"] = aligned.returncode
        if aligned.returncode != 0:
            errors.append("zipalign verification failed")

    if not banner_verified and not banner_invalid_reported:
        errors.append(
            "No compiled TV banner image was identified by resource name or AAPT badging; "
            "resource images: " + ", ".join(resource_images[:20]))
    if not icon_verified and not icon_invalid_reported:
        errors.append(
            "No compiled launcher icon image was identified by resource name or AAPT badging; "
            "resource images: " + ", ".join(resource_images[:20]))

    return {"passed": not errors, "errors": errors, "warnings": warnings, "metrics": metrics}


def main(argv: Iterable[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Verify the ZeroPlay TV ARMv7 APK")
    parser.add_argument("apk", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--json", dest="json_path", type=Path, help="Write the full report to this JSON file")
    parser.add_argument("--require-sdk-tools", action="store_true", help="Fail unless aapt, apksigner and zipalign are available")
    args = parser.parse_args(list(argv) if argv is not None else None)

    report = verify(args.apk, require_sdk_tools=args.require_sdk_tools)
    rendered = json.dumps(report, indent=2)
    print(rendered)
    if args.json_path:
        args.json_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.json_path.write_text(rendered + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return 0 if report["passed"] else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

## `tv/zeroplay-debrid/README.md`

````markdown
# ZeroPlay

ZeroPlay is a keyless movie and series web app with continuous server/addon
discovery. It uses TMDB when the deployment provides a server-side TMDB
credential, otherwise it automatically uses the keyless Cinemeta catalogue
with real artwork. Visitors never enter an API key.

> Real-Debrid features and user API-key setup have been removed.

## Continuous searcher

Open **Sources**. In the normal path it says only **Ready**, **Searching**,
**Found sources**, or **Problem**; use **Find more** to run the same engine.
**Settings → Advanced sources** contains crawler choices, the provider list
and detailed diagnostics. While the app is open, one engine rotates through independent
crawlers:

- Recursive Stremio `addon_catalog` graph crawling, starting with Cinemeta and
  continuing through catalogues exposed by newly identified addons.
- The public, paginated stremio-addons.net API, including addon instances.
- Keyless GitHub repository search with rotating queries/pages and automatic
  rate-limit backoff.
- GitHub manifest/server probing (homepage, GitHub Pages, README manifest
  links and common repository manifest paths).
- Provider/source JSON feeds and user-added discovery seeds.
- Website-server profile refresh.
- A server-identification queue for candidates found by the other crawlers.
- Title-scoped checks of identified stream candidates from public addon catalogs.
- Rotating health-check batches.

ZeroPlay does not impose a provider-registry cap. The provider list is merely
rendered in pages for browser performance. Browser storage, CORS, upstream
availability and public API rate limits remain external limits.

## Server identification before installation

Finding a URL is not enough. The crawler identifies what the endpoint is
before installing it. For a Stremio-style server it validates the manifest and
records:

- server/addon name and version;
- declared resources (`stream`, `catalog`, `meta`, `subtitles`,
  `addon_catalog`);
- movie/series support;
- catalogue ID prefixes such as IMDb `tt` or `tmdb`;
- searchable catalogues;
- episode capability;
- identification confidence and the checks that passed.

Non-stream capabilities and providers explicitly added by the user keep the
existing install behavior. Stream providers discovered through public addon
catalogues are held as title-scoped candidates: ZeroPlay checks at most 100
identified candidates for the requested movie/episode per search, rotates the
batch across larger candidate registries, and keeps no more than 12 candidate
checks in flight at once. A candidate is promoted into the installed
provider list only when it returns a direct stream that passes the app's
existing title/episode identity checks. This bounded candidate scan runs in
parallel with the 100-worker installed-provider search, using the current
candidate-registry snapshot. The title search never starts the continuous
crawler; the crawler has its own timer and updates the registry independently.
Newly discovered servers are available to the next title search. Unmatched
candidates are not imported into playback sources. Manual seeds and configured feeds keep
their existing behavior. GitHub projects without a hosted declarative
endpoint/manifest remain candidates; arbitrary repository code is never
executed. Any provider can be
enabled, disabled or removed while the searcher runs. Removed providers are
tombstoned so the crawler does not immediately resurrect them.

## Built-in title identifier

Discovery identifies the **server**. Playback search separately identifies
the **title**. A catalogue item becomes a canonical identity containing:

- TMDB ID and IMDb ID;
- movie/series type;
- canonical, original and alternative titles;
- release year;
- season and episode.

All enabled players, website servers and identified stream providers are
searchable from **Servers with this title**. Providers are queried by exact
IMDb/TMDB ID and can fall back to searchable catalogues using the canonical and
original title variants. Series streams are addressed at the requested season
and episode. Returned website pages, catalogue metas and direct streams are
scored against the canonical identity. Different catalogue IDs or explicit
wrong season/episode markers are hard rejections. The reference regression
fixture “My Heart Beats for Lola Volcán” verifies TMDB `35281`, IMDb
`tt1929755`, the original title “Mi corazón insiste en Lola Volcán”, and its
season/episode-specific catalogue search.

## Multi-tier Server Finder

`server.js` is an optional local Node.js sidecar. Run it with `npm start`; it
serves the existing app and the same-origin `/api/find` route on `0.0.0.0:8787`
(or `PORT`). The browser only calls relative `/api/find` URLs—there is no
`localhost` URL baked into browser code. When ZeroPlay is served by Vercel or
Netlify, the matching serverless route uses the same candidate-discovery core
as a bounded async pool; the local process uses Node `worker_threads`. If the
API is unavailable, the existing in-browser provider/catalog/GitHub crawlers
continue independently.

The discovery pool uses three bounded, allowlisted sources: the Stremio addon
catalogue, the Cinemeta community/official addon graph, and GitHub repository
metadata/README links. It inspects public HTTPS manifests only, never executes
GitHub-discovered code, and returns candidates—not streams or installable
providers. The pool can retain up to 1,000 candidates; each request checks at
most 8 manifests per source (24 candidates total) and the title scanner still
checks at most 100 candidates with 12 workers per pass. A candidate is promoted
only after the existing title-scoped playback scan returns an identity-verified
direct stream for the selected IMDb/TMDB title and episode. The finder reports
source status and uses the app's persisted provider registry as its cache.

This deliberately does not start 1,000 OS threads or import 1,000 arbitrary
scraper modules: that would be unsafe and can overload free-tier hosting. Local
worker-thread fan-out is one worker per discovery source; hosted requests stay
within the bounded async pool. The local `/api/health` endpoint reports the
active mode. Build and run locally with:

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
npm start
```

The server drawer does not dump the whole registry into the player. Direct
providers appear only after they return identity-verified streams for the
selected movie/episode, grouped by server with their actual returned quality
variants. Added websites appear only after an identity-verified lookup match.
The bounded GitHub server finder searches for hosted stream-provider projects
and treats discoveries as candidates, not playable servers. A provider is
promoted only after title-scoped stream verification. The continuously adding
provider crawler runs on its own timer; title lookup never starts it.
Built-in/custom embed templates that can address the exact catalogue ID are
shown in a separate **Exact-ID players** section: a hosting page cannot prove
a cross-origin player's internal library before that player loads, so ZeroPlay
does not call those routes verified. The drawer shows search/rejection counts
while results arrive progressively.

Website servers are lookup-only: ZeroPlay does not import their titles or
covers. The existing catalogue title remains canonical, and the website is
searched for that exact title/episode when playback is requested.

## TV browsing experience

- The floating top bar includes Home, Movies, Series, Categories, Sources,
  Downloads, Settings and Search, plus a slide-in menu.
- `/categories` provides movie and series genre tiles; category chips and
  deep-linkable `?genre=` browse shelves keep the selected category in the URL.
- Home includes category rails in addition to Continue Watching, Watchlist,
  Trending, Popular and Top Rated shelves.
- Cinemeta trailer metadata is preserved on catalogue cards. A muted trailer
  can appear inside the focused/hovered poster block, the featured hero and
  the title detail backdrop. Rail/page scrolling starts a preview only after
  scrolling settles and only when a trailer key is already known.
- Trailer previews are one-at-a-time and respect the playback setting, Data
  Saver, save-data/2G connections, reduced-motion preferences, tab visibility
  and an already-open player.
- TV-style arrow-key spatial navigation moves predictably between cards,
  buttons, menus and player controls. `Enter` opens a title and `P` quick-plays
  a focused card.

### Android TV / Xiaomi TV Box S (3rd Gen)

The separate app in `tv/android-tv` targets the MDZ-32-AA box's 32-bit
`armeabi-v7a` userspace and 2 GB RAM. On that shell, ZeroPlay changes from a
dense web layout into a couch-first interface:

- an existing Continue Watching row is shown before the featured hero for
  instant resume;
- poster rows and category artwork are much larger, while ratings/year text,
  filter forms, text category lists, extra hero actions and footer chrome are
  removed from the normal path;
- Sources and Settings open one useful job at a time, with source counters and
  playback internals behind Advanced/Diagnostics;
- native Back, Menu, Search and media keys are forwarded predictably, and
  trim-memory signals stop previews/nonessential artwork work;
- posters/backdrops use TV-sized renditions and are completed automatically
  by keyless Cinemeta/MetaHub, TVmaze, AniList and Apple iTunes endpoints.
  No visitor artwork API key exists or is required.

Build and verification details are in `../android-tv/README.md`.

## Settings and switches

The menu drawer has a deliberately short **Quick settings** list: automatic
source search, trailer previews, failover, downloads, autoplay-next, missing
poster lookup, and (inside the TV shell) the lighter-TV performance switch.
The full Settings page retains the less common controls. The full **Settings** page (`/settings`)
contains the same shared settings plus:

- **Add Website** for lookup-only website servers and optional advanced URL
  templates;
- the Advanced sources controls, discovery seeds, crawler choices, provider
  feed and diagnostics;
- separate switches for trailers, automatic switching, confirmed-stall
  switching, Embedwave automatic failover, FastStream preload/API probing,
  DNS warm-up, health sorting, downloads, multithreading, M3U extraction,
  download auto-resume/auto-save/link-refresh/retention, autoplay-next,
  reduced motion, compact cards and the category strip; display preferences
  also include dark, OLED-black, warm-violet and light themes, larger text
  and high contrast;
- FastStream configuration for the direct-stream engine, preload mode,
  preferred quality, default source, buffer target, embed-load and
  confirmed-stall timing, safe range-priming workers/chunks/budget, the file
  cap and Data Saver;
- download defaults for threads, part size and concurrent jobs;
- settings export/import and playback health/server-cache clearing.

Switch changes save immediately and synchronize between the menu, Settings,
player and Downloads. The numeric FastStream/download controls are clamped
to safe ranges when read and when saved.

## Downloads and M3U extraction

A **Download** button appears on the title/detail actions, beside every
episode in the episode selector, in the player, and beside downloadable
direct variants in **Servers with this title**. Episode download buttons use
that episode's exact canonical identity; they never reuse whichever episode
happens to be selected for playback.

Downloads are offered only when an identified server returns a direct media
file or an M3U/HLS playlist for the exact movie/episode. The **Downloads**
page (`/downloads`) is the job manager and M3U extractor:

- Known-size files with genuine HTTP Range/`206` support download in parallel
  chunks (1–8 configured threads). Completed chunks are stored in IndexedDB,
  so Pause and a browser restart can resume only the missing chunks.
- HLS media playlists download independently fetchable segments in parallel
  and assemble them in playlist order, including ordered `EXT-X-MAP` sections
  and byte-range segments. Fetchable AES-128 segments are decrypted in the
  browser.
- If a host does not confirm Range support, ZeroPlay saves sequential parts
  and attempts a validated range resume. If the host restarts with HTTP 200
  or returns the wrong offset, ZeroPlay says so instead of splicing unlike
  responses together.
- Expired direct links can be re-found only when the replacement file has the
  same known size; expired HLS links only when the segment path sequence is
  the same. Otherwise the job stops safely.
- Completed jobs can be saved to the device or played from the assembled
  browser file when the browser supports that container. Jobs can be paused,
  resumed, retried, copied, deleted or cleared in bulk.
- The M3U extractor accepts a website/watch page, a hosted M3U/M3U8 URL, or
  pasted playlist text. It lists variants, segment counts and playlist
  duration, and can inspect, copy, play or download a hosted playlist. A
  pasted media playlist without its real hosted URL is parsed locally only;
  ZeroPlay does not pretend the app URL is a downloadable playlist.
- The configured file cap (hard maximum 5 GB) is checked before download when
  size or HLS bandwidth/duration makes it estimable, and while unknown-size
  parts are being stored.

Cross-origin embedded players cannot be downloaded from the parent page.
When only embeds are returned, ZeroPlay explains that limitation instead of
offering a dead download button.

## Playback rules

- VidStuck, ZXCStream and Embedwave remain the built-in embed focus.
- Embedwave is always last resort. Automatic failover into Embedwave is off
  by default and has its own switch; without it, ZeroPlay stops and lets the
  user choose Embedwave manually from Servers.
- An embed iframe merely loading is **not** treated as successful playback.
  ZeroPlay separates “player page loaded” from provider progress messages
  whose timestamp actually advances. A page that never loads can fail over
  after the configured 15–60 second timeout; a loaded VidStuck/ZXCStream page
  is left alone for its own server checks/Play button, and only confirmed
  timestamp progress can start the 30–120 second stall clock. Embed referrer
  policy matches the upstream players (`no-referrer` for Embedwave,
  `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` for the others).
- Every playback mode opens in the same ZeroPlay shell. The shell keeps Back,
  Servers, Details, episode controls and Close in the parent page so a
  cross-origin iframe cannot trap the whole interface.
- Native and FastStream-API playback expose ZeroPlay play/pause, seek, ±10
  seconds, volume/mute, playback speed, quality, PiP and fullscreen controls.
  Cross-origin embeds expose an explicit **Video controls** focus button
  because their internal controls cannot be driven from the parent page.
- FastStream is the default player for every verified direct stream returned by
  a selected or discovered server. ZeroPlay first attempts FastStream's
  EmbedAPI: when the hosted build sends `ready`, it subscribes and drives
  FastStream with `load`, seek, volume, rate, PiP and
  `getLevels`/`setVideoLevel`. If the API is unavailable, the hosted FastStream
  player is used; only an explicit ZeroPlay player selection or a guarded
  compatibility fallback uses the native responsive `<video>` engine.
- **FastStream — default**, **Automatic fallback — FastStream first**, and
  **ZeroPlay responsive player** remain selectable in **Settings → Advanced
  playback**.
- Quality selection is real where the engine exposes it: FastStream levels
  for API playback and actual returned direct-stream variants for file
  playback. A single fixed file has only its source quality. For third-party
  embeds the selector records a preference and says that the embed chooses its
  actual internal quality.
- Switching a direct quality/server preserves the current timestamp where the
  active engine reports it.
- Failover searches the title-specific server set instead of cycling blindly
  through every registered source. The automatic-switching master switch also
  gates automatic direct-variant fallback; manual quality/server choices are
  unaffected. Native direct playback uses the same confirmed-progress rule
  before a stall can trigger switching.
- Progress persistence and playback UI updates are throttled. Direct priming
  accepts only genuine `206` range responses and uses the configured
  FastStream limits (1–4 workers, chunk size, data budget and buffer target).
  Continuous discovery cycles are deferred while the player is open.
- Torrent and external-player streams are hidden.
- Known direct files over the selected cap are rejected; the hard maximum is
  5 GB.
- No external players are used.

## Catalogue and keys

There are no user API-key fields. A browser cannot safely mint valid
third-party account keys, so ZeroPlay uses keyless public APIs and, for TMDB,
only an optional deployer-owned server environment secret:

- `TMDB_API_KEY`, or
- `TMDB_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

If neither deployment variable exists, Cinemeta is used automatically. The
GitHub, stremio-addons.net and Cinemeta crawlers require no visitor key.

## Deployment

### Vercel

Use this folder as the project root (`tv/zeroplay-debrid` in this repository).
The serverless functions are:

- `api/tmdb.js` — optional server-side TMDB proxy;
- `api/extract.js` — guarded website lookup, JSON relay, validated playlist
  text (`mode=text`) and page/playlist M3U extraction (`mode=m3u`). Remote
  documents are read with a streamed 1.5 MB safety cap; oversized playlists
  are refused for `mode=text` instead of being silently truncated.

### Netlify

`netlify.toml` publishes this folder and routes `/api/tmdb` and
`/api/extract` to the matching functions in `netlify/functions/`.

An optional TMDB environment variable can be set by the deployer; it is not
required for the live keyless catalogue.

## Tests

```bash
npm test
npm run build
```

`npm test` runs identity/discovery, crawler, regression, TV/player, and
download/M3U/settings suites. The download suite exercises the real inline
functions with mocked range/HLS responses rather than only checking that
buttons exist.

## Honest limitations

- Continuous crawling runs while the web app/tab (or a future server worker)
  is running.
- A discovered GitHub repository without a hosted endpoint cannot be turned
  into a working in-browser server merely from source code.
- A website that requires login, CAPTCHA, DRM, private APIs or JavaScript-only
  private routes may not expose a usable public result.
- FastStream/ZeroPlay cannot control quality or internals inside unrelated
  cross-origin embed players.
- Exact-ID embed routes are addressable playback routes, not proof that the
  third-party player's internal catalogue contains a title; verified direct
  and website matches are therefore labelled separately.
- Trailer previews depend on catalogue trailer metadata and YouTube embed
  availability; titles without a trailer keep their poster/backdrop.
- The 5 GB cap is exact when usable size metadata/headers exist; otherwise
  the app labels size as unknown instead of inventing it. Unknown-size
  downloads are stopped as stored bytes reach the configured cap.
- Browser downloads require the remote host to permit CORS. Parallelism and
  pause/resume additionally require HTTP Range/`206` responses or
  independently fetchable HLS segments. Browser/IndexedDB quota can still
  limit how much can be stored; if IndexedDB is unavailable, the in-memory
  fallback cannot survive a browser restart.
- HLS downloads do not support DRM or SAMPLE-AES, live playlists without an
  end marker cannot be completed as one file, separate audio renditions are
  not muxed into the selected video playlist, and DASH is playback-only in
  this downloader. An assembled `.ts` may need to be saved and played by a
  media player that supports MPEG-TS if the browser itself cannot play it.
- Public crawlers can be rate-limited or changed by their operators.

ZeroPlay hosts no media files. This product uses the TMDB API when configured
but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.
````

## `tv/zeroplay-debrid/api/extract.js`

```javascript
/* ZeroPlay — website title lookup + watch resolver (Vercel Function)
 *
 * mode=profile : inspect a user-added website only to discover how its public
 *                search works. It does not import that site's titles/covers.
 * mode=find    : check whether an existing catalogue title exists on that
 *                website, then resolve its public watch/embed/direct URL.
 * mode=watch   : inspect one known watch page for public embed/direct URLs.
 * mode=json    : fetch a JSON URL server-side (CORS fallback for addons).
 * mode=text    : return a validated M3U/M3U8 playlist without truncation.
 * mode=m3u     : extract M3U/M3U8 links/variants from a page or playlist.
 *
 * Safety: http(s) only, private/loopback hosts blocked, 1.5 MB response cap,
 * bounded search requests and timeouts. This parses public pages only; it
 * does not log in, bypass paywalls, solve CAPTCHAs, or bypass DRM.
 */
'use strict';

const MAX_BYTES = 1500000;
const UA = 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/126.0 Safari/537.36';
const SEARCH_PLACEHOLDER = '__ZP_Q__';
const BLOCKED_PATH = /\/(login|register|signup|filter|search|genre|genres|tag|tags|category|categories|type|types|year|years|status|user|profile|dmca|terms|privacy|contact|about|home)(\/|\?|$)/i;

function guardUrl(raw) {
  let u;
  try { u = new URL(String(raw || '')); } catch { return null; }
  if (u.protocol !== 'https:' && u.protocol !== 'http:') return null;
  const h = u.hostname.toLowerCase();
  if (h === 'localhost' || h.endsWith('.local') || h.endsWith('.internal')) return null;
  if (/^(127\.|10\.|192\.168\.|169\.254\.|0\.)/.test(h)) return null;
  if (/^172\.(1[6-9]|2\d|3[01])\./.test(h)) return null;
  if (h === '::1' || h === '[::1]') return null;
  if (!h.includes('.')) return null;
  return u;
}

function canonicalHost(host) {
  return String(host || '').toLowerCase().replace(/^www\./, '');
}

function sameSite(a, b) {
  try { return canonicalHost(new URL(a).hostname) === canonicalHost(new URL(b).hostname); } catch { return false; }
}

async function fetchDocument(url, wantJson, timeoutMs) {
  const ctl = new AbortController();
  const to = setTimeout(() => ctl.abort(), timeoutMs || 10000);
  try {
    const r = await fetch(url, {
      signal: ctl.signal,
      redirect: 'follow',
      headers: { 'User-Agent': UA, Accept: wantJson ? 'application/json,text/plain,*/*' : 'text/html,application/xhtml+xml,*/*' },
    });
    if (!r.ok) throw new Error('HTTP ' + r.status);
    const finalUrl = r.url || url;
    const final = guardUrl(finalUrl);
    if (!final) throw new Error('Blocked redirect');
    let buf;
    if (r.body && typeof r.body.getReader === 'function') {
      const reader = r.body.getReader();
      const chunks = [];
      let total = 0;
      while (total <= MAX_BYTES) {
        const part = await reader.read();
        if (part.done) break;
        if (!part.value) continue;
        const room = MAX_BYTES + 1 - total;
        const slice = part.value.byteLength > room ? part.value.subarray(0, room) : part.value;
        chunks.push(Buffer.from(slice));
        total += slice.byteLength;
        if (part.value.byteLength > room || total > MAX_BYTES) {
          try { await reader.cancel(); } catch {}
          break;
        }
      }
      buf = Buffer.concat(chunks, total);
    } else {
      buf = Buffer.from(await r.arrayBuffer());
    }

function embedScore(url) {

function isM3uText(text) {
  return /^#EXTM3U/i.test(String(text || '').trim());
}

function m3uPlaylistInfo(text, base) {

  const variants = [];
  let pendingVariant = false;
  let pendingDuration = 0;
  let segmentCount = 0;
  let duration = 0;
  let encrypted = false;
  let live = true;
  for (const line of lines) {
    if (!line) continue;
    if (line.startsWith('#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:')) { pendingVariant = true; continue; }
    if (line.startsWith('#EXTINF:')) { pendingDuration = Number(line.slice(8).split(',')[0]) || 0; continue; }

function extractM3u(text, base) {

    const summary = isMaster ? `${info.variants.length} variants` : `${info.segmentCount} segments`;

      : `${info.duration} sec playlist duration${info.encrypted ? ' · encryption declared' : ' · unencrypted'}${info.live ? ' · live/no end marker' : ''}`;

      title: 'M3U playlist',
      playlists: [{ url: base, label: isMaster ? 'M3U master playlist' : 'M3U media playlist', summary, detail }]

function extractCandidateIds(candidate) {

function titleScore(candidate, targets, opts) {

  const candidateIds = extractCandidateIds(candidate);
  const wantedImdb = String(opts.imdb || opts.imdbId || '').toLowerCase();
  const wantedTmdb = Number(opts.tmdb || opts.tmdbId || 0) || null;
  const epInfo = explicitEpisodeInfo([candidate && candidate.title, candidate && candidate.slugTitle, candidate && candidate.url].filter(Boolean).join(' '));
  const episodeConflict = (opts.type === 'tv' || opts.type === 'series') && ((epInfo.season != null && epInfo.season !== Number(opts.season || 1)) || (epInfo.episode != null && epInfo.episode !== Number(opts.episode || 1)));
  if (wantedImdb && candidateIds.imdbId && wantedImdb !== candidateIds.imdbId) return 0;
  if (wantedTmdb && candidateIds.tmdbId && wantedTmdb !== candidateIds.tmdbId) return 0;

      else if (cand.startsWith(target + ' ')) {

  const reasons = [];
  const wantedImdb = String(opts.imdb || '').toLowerCase();
  const wantedTmdb = Number(opts.tmdb || 0) || null;
  let hardReject = false;
  if (wantedImdb && candidateIds.imdbId && wantedImdb !== candidateIds.imdbId) { hardReject = true; reasons.push('different IMDb id'); }
  else if (wantedImdb && candidateIds.imdbId === wantedImdb) reasons.push('exact IMDb id');
  if (wantedTmdb && candidateIds.tmdbId && wantedTmdb !== candidateIds.tmdbId) { hardReject = true; reasons.push('different TMDB id'); }
  else if (wantedTmdb && candidateIds.tmdbId === wantedTmdb) reasons.push('exact TMDB id');
  if ((opts.type === 'tv' || opts.type === 'series') && ((episodeInfo.season != null && episodeInfo.season !== Number(opts.season || 1)) || (episodeInfo.episode != null && episodeInfo.episode !== Number(opts.episode || 1)))) {
    hardReject = true; reasons.push('different season/episode');
  }
  if (score >= 95) reasons.push('exact title');
  else if (score >= 80) reasons.push('verified title');

    const years = ([candidate && candidate.title, candidate && candidate.url].filter(Boolean).join(' ').match(/\b(19\d{2}|20\d{2})\b/g) || []);

    score: hardReject ? 0 : score,
    verdict: hardReject ? 'rejected' : score >= 95 ? 'exact' : score >= 80 ? 'verified' : score >= 65 ? 'possible' : 'rejected',
    accepted: !hardReject && score >= 80,
    hardReject,

function candidateSlugTitle(url) {
  try {
    const parts = new URL(url).pathname.split('/').filter(Boolean).map(x => { try { return decodeURIComponent(x); } catch { return x; } });
    const useful = parts.filter(p => !/^(anime|movie|movies|tv|series|show|watch|detail|info|play|title|video|episode|ep-\d+|\d+)$/i.test(p));
    return normalizeTitle(useful.join(' ').replace(/[-_]+/g, ' '));
  } catch { return ''; }
}

function parseResultLinks(html, base) {
  const byUrl = new Map();
  const anchorRe = /<a\s[^>]*href\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"[^>]*>([\s\S]{0,1200}?)<\/a>/gi;
  for (const m of html.matchAll(anchorRe)) {
    const hrefRaw = decodeEntities(m[1] || '');
    if (!hrefRaw || hrefRaw.startsWith('#') || /^javascript:/i.test(hrefRaw)) continue;
    let url = abs(hrefRaw, base);
    if (!url || !guardUrl(url) || !sameSite(url, base)) continue;
    try {
      const u = new URL(url);
      u.hash = '';
      if (u.pathname === '/' || BLOCKED_PATH.test(u.pathname + u.search)) continue;
      url = u.href;
    } catch { continue; }
    const inner = m[2] || '';
    const imgTag = (inner.match(/<img\s[^>]*>/i) || [])[0] || '';
    const openTag = m[0].slice(0, m[0].indexOf('>') + 1);
    const title = decodeEntities(stripTags(attr(openTag, 'title') || attr(imgTag, 'alt') || inner)).slice(0, 140);
    const slug = candidateSlugTitle(url);
    if ((!title || title.length < 2) && (!slug || slug.length < 2)) continue;
    const prior = byUrl.get(url);
    if (!prior || (!prior.title && title) || (title && title.length < prior.title.length && normalizeTitle(title).length >= 2)) {
      byUrl.set(url, { title: title || (prior && prior.title) || '', slugTitle: slug, url });

  }

function addTemplate(out, template, base) {
  if (!template) return;
  let t = String(template).replace(/%7B/gi, '{').replace(/%7D/gi, '}');
  t = t.replaceAll(SEARCH_PLACEHOLDER, '{q}');
  if (!t.includes('{q}') && !t.includes('{slug}')) return;
  const probe = t.replace('{q}', 'test').replace('{slug}', 'test');
  const u = guardUrl(abs(probe, base));
  if (!u || !sameSite(u.href, base)) return;
  if (!out.includes(t)) out.push(t);
}

function searchTemplatesFromHtml(html, base) {
  const out = [];
  const searchNames = new Set(['q', 'query', 'search', 'keyword', 'keywords', 's', 'title', 'text', 'term', 'name']);
  for (const fm of html.matchAll(/<form\b[^>]*>[\s\S]{0,4000}?<\/form>/gi)) {
    const form = fm[0];
    const open = form.slice(0, form.indexOf('>') + 1);
    if (/method\s*=\s*["']?post/i.test(open)) continue;
    const inputs = [...form.matchAll(/<input\b[^>]*>/gi)].map(x => x[0]);
    const searchInput = inputs.find(tag => {
      const name = attr(tag, 'name').toLowerCase();
      return searchNames.has(name) || /^search$/i.test(attr(tag, 'type')) || /search/i.test(attr(tag, 'placeholder'));
    });
    if (!searchInput) continue;
    const name = attr(searchInput, 'name') || 'q';
    const action = abs(attr(open, 'action') || base, base);
    const u = guardUrl(action);
    if (!u) continue;
    for (const tag of inputs) {
      const n = attr(tag, 'name');
      if (!n || n === name) continue;
      if (/hidden/i.test(attr(tag, 'type'))) u.searchParams.set(n, attr(tag, 'value') || '');

    const raw = abs(decodeEntities(m[1]), base);
    const u = guardUrl(raw);
    if (!u) continue;
    for (const key of ['keyword', 'q', 'query', 'search', 's', 'title']) {
      if (u.searchParams.has(key)) { u.searchParams.set(key, SEARCH_PLACEHOLDER); addTemplate(out, u.href, base); break; }
    }
  }
  return out.slice(0, 8);
}

function commonSearchTemplates(siteUrl) {
  const u = guardUrl(siteUrl);
  if (!u) return [];
  const roots = new Set();
  roots.add(u.origin);
  try { roots.add(new URL('./', u.href).href.replace(/\/$/, '')); } catch {}
  const suffixes = ['/search?keyword={q}', '/search?q={q}', '/search?query={q}', '/filter?keyword={q}', '/?s={q}', '/search/{slug}', '/search/{q}'];
  const out = [];
  for (const root of roots) for (const suffix of suffixes) {
    const t = root + suffix;
    if (!out.includes(t)) out.push(t);
  }
  return out;
}

function buildSearchUrl(template, query) {
  return String(template || '')
    .replaceAll('{slug}', slugTitle(query))
    .replaceAll('{q}', encodeURIComponent(query));
}

async function profileSite(rawUrl) {
  const u = guardUrl(rawUrl);
  if (!u) throw new Error('Invalid or blocked URL');
  const docs = [];
  const first = await fetchDocument(u.href, false, 8000);
  docs.push(first);
  let templates = searchTemplatesFromHtml(first.text, first.finalUrl);
  if (!templates.length && !sameSite(first.finalUrl, u.origin + '/')) {
    try {
      const root = await fetchDocument(u.origin + '/', false, 8000);
      docs.push(root);
      templates = searchTemplatesFromHtml(root.text, root.finalUrl);
    } catch {}
  } else if (!templates.length && u.pathname !== '/') {
    try {
      const root = await fetchDocument(u.origin + '/', false, 8000);
      docs.push(root);
      templates = [...new Set([...templates, ...searchTemplatesFromHtml(root.text, root.finalUrl)])];
    } catch {}
  }
  if (!templates.length) templates = commonSearchTemplates(u.href).slice(0, 4);
  const embedHosts = [...new Set(docs.flatMap(d => iframeHosts(d.text)))];
  return {
    ok: true,
    mode: 'profile',
    url: first.finalUrl,
    origin: u.origin,
    lookup: 'dynamic-title-search',
    searchTemplate: templates[0] || '',
    searchTemplates: templates.slice(0, 5),
    embedHosts,
  };
}

function adjustEpisodeInUrl(url, season, episode) {
  let out = String(url || '');
  const ep = episode == null ? null : String(episode);
  const se = season == null ? null : String(season);
  if (ep != null) {
    out = out.replace(/([?&](?:ep|episode|episode_id)=)\d+/i, '$1' + ep);
    out = out.replace(/(\/(?:ep|episode)[-_/])(\d+)(\/?(?:[?#].*)?)$/i, '$1' + ep + '$3');
    out = out.replace(/(-ep(?:isode)?-)(\d+)(\/?(?:[?#].*)?)$/i, '$1' + ep + '$3');
  }
  if (se != null && ep != null) {
    out = out.replace(/(\/season[-_/])(\d+)(\/episode[-_/])(\d+)/i, '$1' + se + '$3' + ep);
    out = out.replace(/(\/)(\d{1,3})\/(\d{1,4})(\/?(?:[?#].*)?)$/i, (m, slash, oldSeason, oldEpisode, tail) => {
      return /\/(tv|series|show|anime)\//i.test(out) ? slash + se + '/' + ep + tail : m;
    });
  }
  return out;
}

function episodeCandidateUrls(url, episode) {
  if (episode == null) return [];
  try {
    const u = new URL(url);
    if (/(?:\/(?:ep|episode)[-_/]\d+|-ep(?:isode)?-\d+|[?&](?:ep|episode|episode_id)=\d+)/i.test(u.href)) return [];
    const path = u.pathname.replace(/\/+$/, '');
    if (!path || path === '/') return [];
    return [u.origin + path + '/ep-' + episode, u.origin + path + '/episode-' + episode];
  } catch { return []; }
}

function findEpisodeUrl(html, base, season, episode) {
  if (episode == null) return '';
  const stripEpisode = value => {
    try {
      const u = new URL(value);
      return u.origin + u.pathname
        .replace(/\/(?:ep|episode)[-_/]\d+(?:\/|$)/i, '/')
        .replace(/-ep(?:isode)?-\d+(?:\/|$)/i, '/')
        .replace(/\/$/, '');
    } catch { return ''; }
  };
  const baseKey = stripEpisode(base);
  let best = '', bestScore = -1;
  for (const m of String(html || '').matchAll(/<a\s[^>]*href\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"[^>]*>([\s\S]{0,500}?)<\/a>/gi)) {
    const url = abs(decodeEntities(m[1] || ''), base);
    if (!url || !guardUrl(url) || !sameSite(url, base)) continue;
    const openTag = m[0].slice(0, m[0].indexOf('>') + 1);
    const text = normalizeTitle(attr(openTag, 'title') || stripTags(m[2] || ''));
    const epMatches = [
      new RegExp('/(?:ep|episode)[-_/]' + episode + '(?:[/?#]|$)', 'i'),
      new RegExp('-ep(?:isode)?-' + episode + '(?:[/?#]|$)', 'i'),
      new RegExp('[?&](?:ep|episode|episode_id)=' + episode + '(?:[&#]|$)', 'i'),
    ].some(re => re.test(url));
    const textMatches = text === String(episode) || text === 'episode ' + episode || text === 'ep ' + episode;
    if (!epMatches && !textMatches) continue;
    let score = epMatches ? 60 : 40;
    if (baseKey && stripEpisode(url) === baseKey) score += 25;
    const seasonInUrl = explicitSeason(url);
    if (seasonInUrl != null) score += seasonInUrl === Number(season || 1) ? 20 : -50;
    if (score > bestScore) { bestScore = score; best = url; }
  }
  return bestScore >= 40 ? best : '';
}
function cleanVariants(query) {
  const values = [query.title, ...(Array.isArray(query.alternatives) ? query.alternatives : []), query.alt].flatMap(v => String(v || '').split('|'));
  const seen = new Set(), out = [];
  for (const v of values) {
    const clean = String(v || '').replace(/\s*\(source test\)\s*$/i, '').trim().slice(0, 140);
    const key = normalizeTitle(clean);
    if (clean && key && !seen.has(key)) { seen.add(key); out.push(clean); }
  }
  return out.slice(0, 12);
}

async function resolveMatchedWatch(matchUrl, query) {
  const isTv = query.type === 'tv' || query.type === 'series';
  const adjusted = isTv ? adjustEpisodeInUrl(matchUrl, query.season || 1, query.episode || 1) : matchUrl;
  const attempts = [...new Set([adjusted, matchUrl].filter(Boolean))];
  let last = null;

  for (const candidateUrl of attempts) {
    const safe = guardUrl(candidateUrl);
    if (!safe) continue;
    try {
      const doc = await fetchDocument(safe.href, false, 8000);
      let watch = parseWatch(doc.text, doc.finalUrl);
      let watchUrl = doc.finalUrl;
      let resolvedEpisode = false;
      if (isTv && !watch.embed && !watch.direct.length) {
        let episodeUrl = findEpisodeUrl(doc.text, doc.finalUrl, query.season || 1, query.episode || 1);
        if (episodeUrl) resolvedEpisode = true;
        if (episodeUrl && episodeUrl !== doc.finalUrl) {
          const epDoc = await fetchDocument(episodeUrl, false, 8000);
          watch = parseWatch(epDoc.text, epDoc.finalUrl);
          watchUrl = episodeUrl;
        } else if (!episodeUrl) {
          for (const inferredUrl of episodeCandidateUrls(doc.finalUrl, query.episode || 1)) {
            try {
              const epDoc = await fetchDocument(inferredUrl, false, 7000);
              const epPattern = new RegExp('(?:/(?:ep|episode)[-_/]' + (query.episode || 1) + '(?:[/?#]|$)|-ep(?:isode)?-' + (query.episode || 1) + '(?:[/?#]|$))', 'i');
              const looksLikeEpisode = epPattern.test(epDoc.finalUrl) || !!findEpisodeUrl(epDoc.text, epDoc.finalUrl, query.season || 1, query.episode || 1);
              if (!looksLikeEpisode) continue;
              watch = parseWatch(epDoc.text, epDoc.finalUrl);
              watchUrl = epPattern.test(epDoc.finalUrl) ? epDoc.finalUrl : inferredUrl;
              episodeUrl = watchUrl;
              resolvedEpisode = true;
              break;
            } catch {}
          }
        }
      }
      last = { watch, watchUrl };
      if (watch.direct.length || watch.embed) return last;
      if (resolvedEpisode) return last;
      if (isTv && candidateUrl === adjusted && adjusted !== matchUrl) return last;
    } catch {}
  }
  return last || { watch: { embed: '', embeds: [], direct: [], servers: [], embedHosts: [] }, watchUrl: adjusted || matchUrl };
}

async function findTitleOnSite(rawSiteUrl, rawQuery) {
  const site = guardUrl(rawSiteUrl);
  if (!site) throw new Error('Invalid or blocked site URL');
  const query = {
    title: String(rawQuery.title || rawQuery.q || '').trim(),
    alternatives: rawQuery.alternatives || [],
    alt: rawQuery.alt || '',
    type: rawQuery.type || 'movie',
    year: rawQuery.year || '',
    season: Number(rawQuery.season || 1) || 1,
    episode: Number(rawQuery.episode || 1) || 1,
    imdb: String(rawQuery.imdb || '').toLowerCase(),
    tmdb: Number(rawQuery.tmdb || rawQuery.tmdbId || 0) || null,
  };
  const variants = cleanVariants(query);
  if (!variants.length) throw new Error('A catalogue title is required');

  let homeDoc = null;
  try { homeDoc = await fetchDocument(site.href, false, 7000); } catch {}
  const templates = [];
  if (rawQuery.searchTemplate) addTemplate(templates, rawQuery.searchTemplate, site.href);
  if (homeDoc) for (const t of searchTemplatesFromHtml(homeDoc.text, homeDoc.finalUrl)) addTemplate(templates, t, site.href);
  for (const t of commonSearchTemplates(site.href)) addTemplate(templates, t, site.href);

  let best = null;
  let checked = 0;
  const consider = (candidates, strategy) => {
    for (const candidate of candidates || []) {
      if (!guardUrl(candidate.url) || !sameSite(candidate.url, site.href)) continue;
      const identity = identifyTitleCandidate(candidate, variants, query);
      const score = identity.score;
      checked++;
      const epPattern = /(?:\/(?:ep|episode)[-_/]\d+|-ep(?:isode)?-\d+|[?&](?:ep|episode|episode_id)=\d+)/i;
      const episodeTie = best && score === best.score && (query.type === 'tv' || query.type === 'series') && epPattern.test(candidate.url) && !epPattern.test(best.url);
      if (!best || score > best.score || episodeTie) best = { score, url: candidate.url, strategy, title: candidate.title || candidate.slugTitle || '', identity };
    }
  };

  if (homeDoc) {
    consider(parseResultLinks(homeDoc.text, homeDoc.finalUrl), 'site-home');
    const homeTitle = pageTitle(homeDoc.text).replace(/\s+[-|–—].*$/, '');
    consider([{ title: homeTitle, slugTitle: candidateSlugTitle(homeDoc.finalUrl), url: homeDoc.finalUrl }], 'pasted-page');
  }

  let searchFetches = 0;
  outer:
  for (let vi = 0; vi < variants.length; vi++) {
    if (best && best.score >= 95) break;
    if (vi > 0 && best && best.score >= 80) break;
    for (const template of templates.slice(0, 8)) {
      if (searchFetches >= 10) break outer;
      const searchUrl = guardUrl(buildSearchUrl(template, variants[vi]));
      if (!searchUrl || !sameSite(searchUrl.href, site.href)) continue;
      searchFetches++;
      try {
        const doc = await fetchDocument(searchUrl.href, false, 6000);
        consider(parseResultLinks(doc.text, doc.finalUrl), 'site-search');
        const finalTitle = pageTitle(doc.text).replace(/\s+[-|–—].*$/, '');
        if (!BLOCKED_PATH.test(new URL(doc.finalUrl).pathname)) {
          consider([{ title: finalTitle, slugTitle: candidateSlugTitle(doc.finalUrl), url: doc.finalUrl }], 'search-redirect');
        }
        if (best && best.score >= 98) break outer;
      } catch {}
    }
  }

  if (!best || best.score < 80) {
    return { ok: true, mode: 'find', matched: false, checked, searchFetches, bestScore: best ? best.score : 0, identity: best ? best.identity : null, bestTitle: best ? best.title : '' };
  }

  const resolved = await resolveMatchedWatch(best.url, query);
  const watch = resolved.watch;
  const playUrl = (watch.direct && watch.direct[0]) || watch.embed || resolved.watchUrl;
  return {
    ok: true,
    mode: 'find',
    matched: true,
    checked,
    searchFetches,
    match: { score: best.score, strategy: best.strategy, title: best.title || '' },
    identity: best.identity || null,
    matchedUrl: best.url,
    watchUrl: resolved.watchUrl,
    watchTitle: watch.title || '',
    playUrl,
    embed: watch.embed || '',
    embeds: watch.embeds || [],
    direct: watch.direct || [],
    servers: watch.servers || [],
    embedHosts: watch.embedHosts || [],
    pageFallback: !watch.embed && !(watch.direct && watch.direct.length),
  };
}

async function handle(mode, rawUrl, query) {
  query = query || {};
  const u = guardUrl(rawUrl);
  if (!u) return { status: 400, body: { ok: false, error: 'Invalid or blocked URL' } };
  try {
    if (mode === 'json') {
      const text = await fetchText(u.href, true, 10000);
      let data; try { data = JSON.parse(text); } catch { return { status: 502, body: { ok: false, error: 'Remote did not return JSON' } }; }
      return { status: 200, body: data, raw: true };
    }
    if (mode === 'profile') return { status: 200, body: await profileSite(u.href) };
    if (mode === 'find') {
      const body = await findTitleOnSite(u.href, {
        title: query.q || query.title || '',
        alt: query.alt || '',
        type: query.type || 'movie',
        year: query.year || '',
        season: query.season || 1,
        episode: query.episode || 1,
        imdb: query.imdb || '',
        tmdb: query.tmdb || '',
        searchTemplate: query.searchTemplate || '',
      });
      return { status: 200, body };
    }
    const doc = await fetchDocument(u.href, false, 10000);
    if (mode === 'text') {
      if (!isM3uText(doc.text)) return { status: 415, body: { ok: false, error: 'Remote did not return an M3U/M3U8 playlist' } };
      if (doc.truncated) return { status: 413, body: { ok: false, error: 'Remote playlist is larger than the resolver safety limit' } };
      return { status: 200, body: { ok: true, mode: 'text', url: doc.finalUrl, text: doc.text } };
    }
    if (mode === 'm3u') {
      return { status: 200, body: { ok: true, mode: 'm3u', url: doc.finalUrl, truncated: !!doc.truncated, ...extractM3u(doc.text, doc.finalUrl) } };
    }
    return { status: 200, body: { ok: true, mode: 'watch', url: doc.finalUrl, truncated: !!doc.truncated, ...parseWatch(doc.text, doc.finalUrl) } };
  } catch (e) {
    return { status: 502, body: { ok: false, error: 'Site lookup failed: ' + (e && e.message || e) } };
  }
}

module.exports = async function handler(req, res) {
  res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json; charset=utf-8');
  res.setHeader('X-Content-Type-Options', 'nosniff');
  res.setHeader('Cache-Control', 'no-store');
  if (req.method !== 'GET') return res.status(405).json({ ok: false, error: 'Method not allowed' });
  const query = req.query || {};
  const mode = String(query.mode || 'profile');
  if (!['profile', 'find', 'watch', 'json', 'text', 'm3u'].includes(mode)) return res.status(400).json({ ok: false, error: 'Unknown mode' });
  const out = await handle(mode, String(query.url || ''), query);
  return res.status(out.status).json(out.body);
};
module.exports._parse = { parseWatch, extractM3u, isM3uText, parseResultLinks, guardUrl, serverNames, normalizeTitle, titleScore, identifyTitleCandidate, explicitEpisodeInfo, extractCandidateIds, searchTemplatesFromHtml, commonSearchTemplates, buildSearchUrl, adjustEpisodeInUrl, findEpisodeUrl, episodeCandidateUrls };
module.exports._find = { profileSite, findTitleOnSite, handle };
```

## `tv/zeroplay-debrid/api/find.js`

```javascript
'use strict';

const { findCandidates, normalizeIdentity } = require('../lib/server-finder/core');

const WINDOW_MS = 60 * 1000;
const MAX_REQUESTS_PER_WINDOW = 8;
const requests = new Map();

function setHeaders(res) {
  res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json; charset=utf-8');
  res.setHeader('X-Content-Type-Options', 'nosniff');
  res.setHeader('Cache-Control', 'private, max-age=20, stale-while-revalidate=30');
  res.setHeader('Vary', 'Origin');
}

function sameOrigin(req) {
  const origin = req.headers && req.headers.origin;
  if (!origin) return true;
  const host = req.headers['x-forwarded-host'] || req.headers.host;
  try { return !!host && new URL(origin).host.toLowerCase() === String(host).split(',')[0].trim().toLowerCase(); }
  catch { return false; }
}

function clientKey(req) {
  const forwarded = req.headers && req.headers['x-forwarded-for'];
  const ip = forwarded ? String(forwarded).split(',')[0].trim() : String(req.socket && req.socket.remoteAddress || 'unknown');
  return ip.slice(0, 80);
}

function allowRequest(req, now = Date.now()) {
  const key = clientKey(req);
  const prior = requests.get(key);
  if (!prior || now - prior.start >= WINDOW_MS) {
    requests.set(key, { start: now, count: 1 });
    return true;
  }
  if (prior.count >= MAX_REQUESTS_PER_WINDOW) return false;
  prior.count++;
  return true;
}

function inputFor(req) {
  if (req.method === 'GET') {
    const query = req.query || {};
    const title = query.q || query.title || '';
    return {
      title, titles: String(query.titles || '').split('|'), type: query.type,
      year: query.year, season: query.season, episode: query.episode,
      imdbId: query.imdbId, tmdbId: query.tmdbId,
    };
  }
  if (req.body && typeof req.body === 'object') return req.body.identity || req.body;
  if (typeof req.body === 'string') {
    try { const body = JSON.parse(req.body); return body.identity || body; } catch { return null; }
  }
  return null;
}

module.exports = async function handler(req, res) {
  setHeaders(res);
  if (!['GET', 'POST'].includes(req.method)) {
    res.setHeader('Allow', 'GET, POST');
    return res.status(405).json({ ok: false, error: 'Method not allowed' });
  }
  if (!sameOrigin(req)) return res.status(403).json({ ok: false, error: 'Same-origin requests only' });
  if (!allowRequest(req)) {
    res.setHeader('Retry-After', '60');
    return res.status(429).json({ ok: false, error: 'Server Finder is rate limited; please retry shortly.' });
  }
  let identity;
  try { identity = normalizeIdentity(inputFor(req)); }
  catch (error) { return res.status(400).json({ ok: false, error: error.message || 'Invalid title identity' }); }
  const result = await findCandidates(identity, {
    limit: 24, maxPerSource: 8, timeoutMs: 4500,
    sourceConcurrency: 6, useWorkerThreads: false,
  });
  return res.status(200).json(result);
};

module.exports._test = { sameOrigin, allowRequest, inputFor, requests, WINDOW_MS, MAX_REQUESTS_PER_WINDOW };
```

## `tv/zeroplay-debrid/api/tmdb.js`

```javascript
/* ZeroPlay RD — TMDB catalog proxy (Vercel Function)
 * Vercel twin of netlify/functions/tmdb.js (same allowlist validation,
 * ported from ZeroPlay web/lib/catalog.cjs). Set ONE env var in Vercel:
 *   TMDB_API_KEY (v3 key)  or  TMDB_ACCESS_TOKEN (v4 bearer).
 * Without it, returns 503 and the site falls back to demo / pasted-key mode.
 */
'use strict';

function endpoint(path) {
  return typeof path === 'string' && (
    /^\/(trending\/all\/(day|week)|movie\/(popular|top_rated|now_playing|upcoming)|tv\/(popular|airing_today|on_the_air)|search\/(multi|person)|watch\/providers\/(movie|tv)|discover\/(movie|tv))$/.test(path) ||
    /^\/(movie|tv)\/[1-9]\d{0,9}(\/season\/\d{1,4})?$/.test(path) ||
    /^\/person\/[1-9]\d{0,9}$/.test(path) ||
    /^\/collection\/[1-9]\d{0,9}$/.test(path)
  );
}

const SORTS = new Set([
  'popularity.desc', 'vote_average.desc', 'vote_count.desc',
  'primary_release_date.desc', 'primary_release_date.asc',
  'first_air_date.desc', 'first_air_date.asc',
  'revenue.desc', 'title.asc', 'name.asc',
]);

function query(params) {
  if (!params || !endpoint(params.path)) throw Error('Unsupported catalog route');
  const allowed = new Set(['query', 'page', 'append_to_response', 'include_image_language', 'watch_region',
    'with_watch_providers', 'with_watch_monetization_types', 'sort_by', 'with_genres', 'with_original_language',
    'primary_release_date.gte', 'primary_release_date.lte', 'first_air_date.gte', 'first_air_date.lte',
    'vote_average.gte', 'vote_count.gte', 'with_runtime.lte', 'with_origin_country']);
  const out = new URLSearchParams({ include_adult: 'false' });
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(params)) {
    if (name === 'path') continue;
    if (!allowed.has(name) || typeof value !== 'string' || value.length > 200) throw Error('Unsupported parameter');
    if (name === 'page' && (!/^[1-9]\d{0,2}$/.test(value) || Number(value) > 500)) throw Error('Invalid page');
    if (name === 'append_to_response' && !['credits,videos,recommendations', 'credits,videos,recommendations,external_ids', 'external_ids', 'credits,videos,recommendations,images', 'videos', 'videos,images', 'images', 'combined_credits'].includes(value)) throw Error('Invalid details request');
    if (name === 'include_image_language' && !/^(?:[a-z]{2}|null)(?:,(?:[a-z]{2}|null)){0,4}$/.test(value)) throw Error('Invalid image language');
    if (name === 'watch_region' && !['PH', 'US', 'GB', 'CA', 'AU', 'IN', 'JP', 'ZA'].includes(value)) throw Error('Invalid region');
    if (name === 'with_watch_providers' && !/^[1-9]\d{0,7}$/.test(value)) throw Error('Invalid provider');
    if (name === 'with_watch_monetization_types' && value !== 'flatrate') throw Error('Invalid availability');
    if (name === 'sort_by' && !SORTS.has(value)) throw Error('Invalid sorting');
    if (name === 'with_genres' && !/^\d{1,8}$/.test(value)) throw Error('Invalid genre');
    if (name === 'with_original_language' && !/^[a-z]{2}$/.test(value)) throw Error('Invalid language');
    if (['primary_release_date.gte', 'primary_release_date.lte', 'first_air_date.gte', 'first_air_date.lte'].includes(name) && !/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(value)) throw Error('Invalid date filter');
    if (name === 'vote_average.gte' && (!/^\d(?:\.\d)?$/.test(value) || Number(value) > 10)) throw Error('Invalid rating');
    if (name === 'vote_count.gte' && !/^\d{1,7}$/.test(value)) throw Error('Invalid vote filter');
    if (name === 'with_runtime.lte' && (!/^\d{1,3}$/.test(value) || Number(value) > 600)) throw Error('Invalid runtime');
    if (name === 'with_origin_country' && !/^[A-Z]{2}$/.test(value)) throw Error('Invalid country');
    out.set(name, value);
  }
  return out;
}

function send(res, status, body, extra = {}) {
  res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json; charset=utf-8');
  res.setHeader('X-Content-Type-Options', 'nosniff');
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(extra)) res.setHeader(k, v);
  return res.status(status).json(body);
}

module.exports = async function handler(req, res) {
  if (req.method !== 'GET') {
    res.setHeader('Allow', 'GET');
    return send(res, 405, { error: 'Method not allowed' });
  }

  const raw = {};
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(req.query || {})) {
    if (Array.isArray(value)) return send(res, 400, { error: 'Invalid catalog request' });
    raw[name] = String(value);
  }

  let params;
  try { params = query(raw); } catch { return send(res, 400, { error: 'Invalid catalog request' }); }

  const v3 = process.env.TMDB_API_KEY;
  const v4 = process.env.TMDB_ACCESS_TOKEN;
  if (!v3 && !v4) return send(res, 503, { error: 'The catalog is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later.', code: 'TMDB_NOT_CONFIGURED' });

  const path = raw.path;
  const url = new URL('https://api.themoviedb.org/3' + path);
  if (v3) params.set('api_key', v3);
  url.search = params.toString();

  try {
    const response = await fetch(url, {
      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000),
      headers: { Accept: 'application/json', ...(v4 && !v3 ? { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + v4 } : {}) },
    });
    if (!response.ok) {
      return send(res, response.status === 429 ? 429 : 502,
        { error: 'The catalog is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later.' },
        response.status === 429 ? { 'Retry-After': '30' } : {});
    }
    const data = await response.json();
    return send(res, 200, data, {
      'Cache-Control': path === '/search/multi' ? 'private, max-age=60' : 'public, max-age=300, s-maxage=300',
    });
  } catch {
    return send(res, 502, { error: 'The catalog is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later.' });
  }
};
```
